$about: The size system of the site: every fluid size comes from this file. build/tokens.mjs reads it (npm run tokens, and before every dev/build), writes each size's value at every Figma Breakpoint mode into design/tokens.json (so Figma gets the same numbers) and one CSS formula per size into src/styles/base/tokens.gen.css. Explained with charts in design/README.md.

One range for everything: a size has its 'from' value on a 320px screen and its 'to' value on a 1440px screen, and goes in a straight line in between (constant outside). Not the screen's width alone: the screen's size is its width, or twice its height minus 400px if that is smaller (height.times, height.minus): every pixel of height a screen lacks counts as two of width. So a phone turned sideways gets the phone sizes, a 1366 × 650 laptop window the sizes of a 900 screen, and every size shrinks together: the ratios between them stay.

Type: a ladder of steps on one base (16px) and one ratio (1.18 on a 320 screen, 1.2 on a 1440 one). A role is two step numbers: its step at 320 and its step at 1440. On phones the levels sit one step apart; on computers they spread. Neighbouring text levels are always at least ×1.18 apart, at every size in between (the ratio of two straight lines can only move from its value at one end to its value at the other). Labels ("label": true) are set apart by case and weight, not size, and are left out of that.
Space: every spacing and radius is two numbers from the ladder below (its value at 320 and at 1440). Roles marked size are measures of a block, not spacing, and need not be on the ladder.
Sizes are written in rem in the CSS (type) or px with the range in rem (space): with the browser's text made bigger, the whole system behaves as on a narrower screen, like the em steps of media.css.

type/card-title.use: the titles of the card stack

type/card-heading.use: titles of cards: tools, publications, royalty; the 404 title

type/lead.use: the text under the hero and the CTA titles

type/card-tag.use: the labels of the card stack: a label, set apart by uppercase, weight and its pill, not by size; it steps from body size to lead size

type/body.use: running text, feature texts, buttons, the footer

type/ui.use: navbar links and button, menu, skip link, footer notes, bylines

aliases.$about: Figma variables the text styles still use, now the same as a role (the site uses only the roles)

section/pad-x.use: side gutter of every section: the content column starts here

stack/pad.use: inset of the full-bleed cards (stack, CTA) from the screen edge, and the gap between stack cards

section/pad-y.use: space above and below a section's content (two sections in a row: twice this between them)

section/gap.use: from a section heading to its content

space/gap-tiles.use: between tiles: features, logos and stats

radius/s.use: tiles: features, logos, stats, ID cards (about 130–250px wide)

radius/m.use: half-column cards: publications, royalty; the padding of the stack cards

radius/l.use: full-column cards: the CTA card (also its side padding), tool cards

space/pad-l.use: padding of the tool cards: one ladder step above their radius (radius/l) — their extra air (design/decisions.json)

card/text-pad.use: padding of a stack card (= radius/m)

card/text-gap.use: a stack card's label → its title

space/text-gap.use: a heading → its text: hero, CTA, tools, publications

space/action-gap.use: a block of text → its button: hero, CTA

tool/gap.use: a tool card's text → its button

feature/gap.use: a feature's icon → its text (at least)

pub/air.use: a publication's text → its footer (at least)

hero/air-top.use: under the navbar, above the hero title (at least)

hero/air-bottom.use: under the hero button, above the team (at least)

space/center-air.use: air at the sides of a centred heading, so a line of big letters is not pressed against the gutter on phones

nav/pad-right.use: a little less than the left on phones: the burger's lines have air of their own

footer/contact-y.use: more air on phones, where the contacts stand in a column

tool/min-h.use: a tool card's least height when text and picture sit side by side

hero/room.use: the hero is never taller than the team picture plus this (its text and air)
